summary: Inline text diff shows the agent's edits to a piece of copy where they sit in the text: the old words struck in red, the new ones beside them in green. Clicking an edit opens a small toolbar to accept or reject it, an edit the agent isn't sure of is marked and says why, and the header can accept or reject everything still waiting.
use: When the agent rewrites copy and people should approve it word by word, not all or nothing.
When the edits are short and read best in place, inside the sentence they change.
When the agent can say it isn't sure of an edit, like a claim that isn't in the brief, so people check that one first.
When most edits are fine and one click should take the rest.
features: `parts` hold the copy in order: plain strings, with edits between them. Each edit has a `key`, the words it replaces (`from`) and the words it suggests (`to`).
An edit with a `note` is marked in amber, and the note shows above its Accept and Reject buttons.
Clicking an edit opens its toolbar under the edit's last line. Accepting keeps the new words and rejecting keeps the old ones, both as plain text.
`decisions` / `defaultDecisions` / `onDecisionsChange` keep what was decided, `accepted` or `rejected` per edit key.
The status under the title counts down the edits left, then says how many were accepted and rejected.
Accept all and Reject all take every edit still waiting. Once none are left, the buttons give way to `doneLabel`.
a11y: Each edit is a button you can reach with Tab and open with Enter or Space, which puts the focus on Accept; ← and → move between Accept and Reject. Its label says which edit it is, the words it replaces and the words it suggests, and `aria-expanded` says whether its toolbar is open.
The toolbar is a dialog labelled "Edit". Escape closes it and puts focus back on the edit, and so does deciding from the keyboard.
The line under the copy is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so the final result is read out.

faq.q: Does it work out the diff between two texts?
faq.a: No. You pass the edits as `parts`, each with the words it replaces and the words it suggests. Your agent decides what changed; the component shows it and records the decisions.

faq.q: How is it different from Change review?
faq.a: Change review is for code: whole files and hunks, kept or undone. Inline text diff is for prose, where each edit is a few words inside a sentence.

faq.q: How do I get the final text?
faq.a: Walk `parts` with the `decisions`: plain strings as they are, `to` for an accepted edit and `from` for a rejected one.
